robin.definition: A bird called robin; European and American robins are different species, commonly with orange or reddish breast coloring.
robin.exampleUsage: The European robin perched on the garden fence.
robin.arabicTranslation: أبو الحناء؛ روبن أمريكي حسب النوع

sparrow.definition: A small bird that often travels in groups.
sparrow.exampleUsage: A sparrow gathered seeds beside the hedge.

blue-jay.definition: A North American bird with blue, white, and black feathers, a crest, and a loud call.
blue-jay.exampleUsage: The blue jay landed on a branch near the feeder.

cardinal.definition: A songbird whose male often has bright red feathers and a pointed crest.
cardinal.exampleUsage: The male northern cardinal perched with its crest raised.

crow.definition: A generally black bird of the crow family, known for varied calls and behavior.
crow.exampleUsage: The crow called from the top of the tree.

pigeon.definition: A bird of the pigeon and dove family, often with a compact body and short neck.
pigeon.exampleUsage: A pigeon walked across the open courtyard.

dove.definition: A bird of the pigeon family, often described as smaller or more slender, although the common names overlap.
dove.exampleUsage: The dove rested on a branch above the path.

finch.definition: Any of numerous small songbirds with short stout bills adapted for crushing seeds.
finch.exampleUsage: The finch cracked a seed with its short bill.

wren.definition: Any of several small active brown birds of the Northern Hemisphere with short upright tails.
wren.exampleUsage: The wren moved through the low shrubs.

starling.definition: A bird of the starling family, often forming flocks; species have different ranges and appearances.
starling.exampleUsage: A flock of starlings gathered before dusk.

duck.definition: A waterbird typically with a broad bill and webbed feet.
duck.exampleUsage: The duck paddled across the pond.

swan.definition: A large long-necked waterbird; plumage may be white or dark depending on species.
swan.exampleUsage: The swan extended its long neck above the water.

goose.definition: A waterbird typically larger than a duck, with a longer neck and webbed feet.
goose.exampleUsage: The goose walked along the edge of the lake.

heron.definition: A long-legged wading bird with a long neck and pointed bill.
heron.exampleUsage: The heron stood in shallow water watching for prey.

pelican.definition: A large waterbird with a long bill and expandable throat pouch.
pelican.exampleUsage: The pelican held a fish in its bill pouch.

flamingo.definition: Large pink to scarlet web-footed wading bird with down-bent bill.
flamingo.exampleUsage: The flamingo fed in the shallow lagoon.

crane.definition: A tall long-legged bird with a long neck, often found near wetlands.
crane.exampleUsage: The crane walked through the wetland on its long legs.

seagull.definition: A common general name for a gull, a water-associated bird with long wings.
seagull.exampleUsage: A seagull flew above the shoreline.

kingfisher.definition: Nonpasserine large-headed bird with a short tail and long sharp bill.
kingfisher.exampleUsage: The kingfisher waited on a branch above the stream.

cormorant.definition: A diving waterbird typically with a long neck and a hooked bill.
cormorant.exampleUsage: The cormorant dived beneath the water.

eagle.definition: A large bird of prey with a strong hooked bill and powerful talons.
eagle.exampleUsage: The eagle circled above the hillside.

hawk.definition: A bird of prey commonly called hawk, with different wing and tail forms depending on species.
hawk.exampleUsage: The hawk watched the open ground from its perch.

falcon.definition: A bird of prey with pointed wings that hunts other animals.
falcon.exampleUsage: The falcon flew past with pointed wings extended.

owl.definition: A bird of prey with forward-facing eyes; many, but not all, species are mainly active at night.
owl.exampleUsage: The owl turned its head toward the sound.

osprey.definition: A large bird of prey adapted mainly to catching fish.
osprey.exampleUsage: The osprey carried a fish toward its nest.

vulture.definition: A bird commonly called vulture, typically feeding largely on carrion.
vulture.exampleUsage: The vulture fed on carrion away from the visitor path.

kite.definition: A bird of prey, many species of which glide with long wings and a forked or angled tail.
kite.exampleUsage: The kite glided over the open field.

harrier.exampleUsage: The harrier searched low over the grassland.
harrier.definition: A bird of prey that flies low over open land while hunting.

kestrel.definition: A small falcon, with several species found in different regions.
kestrel.exampleUsage: The kestrel hovered while watching the ground.

condor.definition: A very large vulture of the Americas, with Andean and California species.
condor.exampleUsage: The condor glided with its broad wings extended.

beak.definition: A bird’s projecting bill, used for feeding and other activities.
beak.exampleUsage: The bird used its beak to pick up a seed.

feather.definition: Branching, hair-like structure that grows on the bodies of birds.
feather.exampleUsage: A loose feather lay beside the path.

wing.definition: A feathered forelimb used by a bird in flight or other movements.
wing.exampleUsage: The bird extended one wing while stretching.

talon.definition: A sharp hooked claw especially on a bird of prey.
talon.exampleUsage: The eagle gripped the branch with a talon.

crest.definition: A tuft of feathers on top of a bird's head.
crest.exampleUsage: The jay raised the crest on its head.

tail.definition: The feathers extending from the rear of a bird's body.
tail.exampleUsage: The bird spread its tail during the turn.

breast.definition: The front of the trunk from the neck to the abdomen.
breast.exampleUsage: The robin's orange breast was visible from the path.

nest.definition: A structure or chosen place used by birds for eggs and raising young.
nest.exampleUsage: The pair carried twigs to the nest.

perch.definition: A branch or bar on which a bird can rest.
perch.exampleUsage: The bird rested on the wooden perch.

fly.definition: To move through the air using wings.
fly.exampleUsage: The birds fly between the trees and the water.

sing.definition: To produce the patterned vocal sounds known as birdsong.
sing.exampleUsage: The songbirds sing from branches above the path.

migrate.exampleUsage: Some birds migrate between breeding and wintering regions.

nest-building.definition: The activity of gathering and arranging materials to make a nest for eggs or young animals.
nest-building.exampleUsage: Nest building began when the pair started carrying twigs.

feed.definition: To eat or provide food, as described in the bird’s activity.
feed.exampleUsage: The parent birds feed their young in the nest.

preen.definition: To clean and arrange feathers with a bird's beak.
preen.exampleUsage: The birds preen their feathers after bathing.

soar.definition: To fly high or glide through the air with little wing movement.
soar.exampleUsage: Large birds can soar above the valley with little wing movement.

dive.definition: To move quickly downward through air or into water.
dive.exampleUsage: Cormorants dive beneath the surface to find food.

flock.definition: A group of birds together in this noun context.
flock.exampleUsage: A flock of geese crossed the sky.

roost.definition: To rest or sleep on a perch, especially as a bird.
roost.exampleUsage: The birds roost in the trees at night.

tree.definition: A tall plant with a woody trunk and branches.
tree.exampleUsage: The tree beside the pond provides shelter.

branch.definition: A woody part that grows from a tree trunk or large branch.
branch.exampleUsage: A bird rested on the upper branch.

birdhouse.exampleUsage: The birdhouse has an entrance suited to the intended nesting species.
birdhouse.definition: A small shelter put outdoors for birds to nest in.

feeder.definition: A container that supplies food for birds.
feeder.exampleUsage: The sanctuary staff refilled the feeder under their management plan.

bath.definition: A shallow container of water where birds drink and clean themselves.
bath.exampleUsage: The bird drank from the shallow bath.

pond.exampleUsage: The pond supports waterbirds and aquatic plants.
pond.definition: A small body of still water, usually smaller than a lake.

wetland.definition: A low area where the land is saturated with water.
wetland.exampleUsage: The protected wetland has water-saturated soil.

meadow.definition: A piece of land covered or mostly covered with grass.
meadow.exampleUsage: The meadow beyond the path is covered mainly with grass.

cliff.definition: A steep wall of rock or earth.
cliff.exampleUsage: Seabirds nested on the cliff above the water.

hedge.definition: A row of bushes planted close together as a boundary.
hedge.exampleUsage: The hedge forms a line of shrubs beside the path.
